candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement) using stroke process-measure data
candidate.educational_objective: Use stroke performance-measure data for structured quality improvement by reviewing eligible cases against the measure's defined criteria and exclusions rather than treating the metric as a substitute for individualized care or as proof of individual fault.

options.A: Review eligible ischemic-stroke cases against the STK-2 discharge-prescribing criteria and documented exclusions to identify process gaps for improvement.
options.B: Assume every ischemic-stroke discharge without an antithrombotic prescription represents an error, regardless of documented reasons for nonprescribing.
options.C: Use the aggregate STK-2 rate to determine which individual bedside nurse caused each missed prescription without reviewing the records.
options.D: Replace individualized discharge decisions with the measure numerator so that all stroke clients receive the same medication plan.

candidate.rationale: The Joint Commission's current STK-2 measure evaluates ischemic-stroke patients prescribed antithrombotic therapy at discharge and includes a pathway for documented reasons for not prescribing therapy. A quality-improvement review should therefore examine eligible cases against the defined measure criteria and exclusions to identify process gaps. B ignores valid documented exclusions, C attributes causation from an aggregate measure without case review, and D misuses a performance measure as a substitute for individualized clinical decision-making.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly defines STK-2 as a stroke process-performance measure based on antithrombotic prescribing at discharge and explicitly accounts for documented reasons for nonprescribing, supporting case review against measure criteria rather than automatic classification of every nonprescription as an error.
candidate.source_document_title: Specifications Manual for Joint Commission National Quality Measures (v2026B) — STK-2: Discharged on Antithrombotic Therapy
candidate.source_locator: Stroke (STK) Measure Information Form, STK-2, version 2026B: Performance Measure Name/Description; numerator and denominator logic; algorithm step 'Reason for Not Prescribing Antithrombotic Therapy at Discharge.' Applies to discharges 07-01-2026 through 12-31-2026.
candidate.stem: A nurse on a hospital stroke quality-improvement team notes that performance on STK-2, Discharged on Antithrombotic Therapy, has declined. Which action best uses this quality-measure information?
